settings.cloudflare.defaults.all-users.h: Otherwise only admins use this token; other users need their own Cloudflare DNS certificate. Existing foreign records are never overwritten.

settings.cloudflare.description: Add an API token once: FloppyGuard then creates the A and AAAA records at Cloudflare for every proxy host, switches the Cloudflare proxy on if you want, and removes the records again when a domain or host is removed.
settings.cloudflare.how.1: Records created by FloppyGuard carry the comment "Managed by FloppyGuard". Only those are changed or deleted.
settings.cloudflare.how.2: An existing record that already points to this server is taken over. One pointing elsewhere is left alone and the host shows a notice.
settings.cloudflare.how.3: Domain removed from the host, switch off or host deleted: the matching records are deleted at Cloudflare. Wildcard domains (*.…) are skipped.
settings.cloudflare.how.4: With the Cloudflare proxy, FloppyGuard takes the visitor IP from CF-Connecting-IP, but only for requests from Cloudflare addresses: forged headers from elsewhere do not count.
settings.cloudflare.manual: Link not working? Do it by hand
settings.cloudflare.manual.1: Cloudflare dashboard → profile (top right) → "API Tokens" → "Create Token".
settings.cloudflare.manual.3: Add the permission Zone · Zone · Read. Under "Zone Resources": Include · All zones (or specific zones).
settings.cloudflare.manual.4: "Continue to summary" → "Create Token" and copy the token shown (it is shown only once).

settings.cloudflare.step1.hint: Opens Cloudflare with all required permissions pre-filled (edit DNS, read zone, all zones, name "FloppyGuard"). Sign in, click "Continue to summary" and then "Create Token". To allow only certain domains, pick them under "Zone Resources".
settings.cloudflare.step3.hint: From now on the Cloudflare switches are preset for new proxy hosts. Turn them on for existing hosts in the host dialog under "Details".

wireguard.agent.allowed-networks-hint: Comma-separated CIDRs this agent may reach via the hub. Empty = full mesh (all other sites). Enforced only on this agent's own gateway, not at the hub: not a security boundary.
wireguard.agent.create-failed: The agent could not be created: {error}
wireguard.agent.delete-confirm: Delete agent {name}? Its token is revoked at once and the gateway is no longer managed from here. If its Freigaben filter is restricted, switch it to open first.
wireguard.agent.delete-force-confirm: {name} cannot be deleted normally: its Freigaben filter is not confirmed as open, and the agent has not reported for over an hour. Delete it anyway? The gateway then keeps its last Freigaben filter (chain FG_IN) until it is removed there by hand.
wireguard.agent.hub-url-hint: Primary / fallback URL all agents use to reach the hub. Pushed to every agent on its next poll — change it here when the hub domain moves.
wireguard.agent.hub-url-invalid: Must be a valid http(s) URL
wireguard.agent.ingress.applied.failed: The agent did NOT apply the ruleset — the filter is not active as shown.
wireguard.agent.ingress.applied.offline: The agent has not reported for more than 5 minutes (offline) — the current ruleset will only be applied once it is back.
wireguard.agent.ingress.applied.pending: The agent has not confirmed the current ruleset yet (applies on its next poll).
wireguard.agent.ingress.applied.unknown: The agent reports no filter status (agent script too old or offline) — whether the filter is active is unknown.
wireguard.agent.ingress.banner.explain: The ingress filter checks traffic that wants to enter this site’s network from the tunnel.
wireguard.agent.ingress.banner.open: All traffic from the tunnel gets through.
wireguard.agent.ingress.banner.open-exce: Ingress filter off – traffic from other sites gets through, except from: {sites} (separated on the hub).
wireguard.agent.ingress.banner.restricte: Only released traffic from the tunnel reaches this network ({count, plural, one {# active rule} other {# active rules}}).
Ingress filter on, but no active rule – all traffic from the tunnel is dropped.
wireguard.agent.ingress.banner.title-off: Ingress filter at this site: off
wireguard.agent.ingress.banner.title-on: Ingress filter at this site: on
wireguard.agent.ingress.catalog.hub-snat: Also carries every hub-LAN host (SNAT to the hub address)
wireguard.agent.ingress.catalog.masquera: This site hides its LAN addresses (masquerade): its traffic arrives with the tunnel address
wireguard.agent.ingress.catalog.unavaila: Names and assistants are unavailable (catalog could not be loaded) — rules can still be entered as IP/CIDR.
wireguard.agent.ingress.check.broad: Hub rules broader than the proxy traffic needs — the hub address also carries every Hetzner-LAN host (SNAT), so these let Mailcow, the web server CT etc. in as well:
wireguard.agent.ingress.check.broad.all-: no port list: every port of the targets is open — limit it to the upstream port(s)
wireguard.agent.ingress.check.egress-not: Hub-originated traffic via the SNAT/tunnel address (e.g. Mailcow → DC) uses no proxy host — it is only checked when listed in /data/hub-egress-flows.json ({count} listed).
wireguard.agent.ingress.check.lead: Compares the proxy hosts and streams on the hub with the rules of this site.
wireguard.agent.ingress.check.link-clien: The bound WireGuard link "{link}" exists but is typed "client", so it is not checked as a site. Set its type to site-to-site if it is a site gateway.
wireguard.agent.ingress.check.link-missi: The bound WireGuard link "{link}" was not found — nothing checked. Re-bind the agent to a link.
wireguard.agent.ingress.check.missing-di: Disabled proxy hosts/streams without a rule (no traffic now, 504 at the hub once enabled):
wireguard.agent.ingress.check.missing-op: Not covered by a rule (informational while the filter is off — with the filter on these targets would be dropped):
wireguard.agent.ingress.check.missing-re: The agent currently drops these proxy host / stream targets (504 at the hub):
wireguard.agent.ingress.check.no-port: port unknown — create the rule by hand with the port(s) used
wireguard.agent.ingress.check.none: No check data for this agent.
wireguard.agent.ingress.check.title: Proxy cross-check
wireguard.agent.ingress.check.unchecked: Not checkable — the upstream is a host name that does not resolve:
wireguard.agent.ingress.check.unused: no proxy host/stream uses this target (maybe manual configuration)
wireguard.agent.ingress.col.name: Name
wireguard.agent.ingress.comfort.missing-: Create {count, plural, one {# rule} other {# rules}} for the missing proxy targets?
wireguard.agent.ingress.comfort.prune-co: Switch off {count, plural, one {# rule} other {# rules}} without a new connection for 30 days?
wireguard.agent.ingress.comfort.prune-do: Switched off {count, plural, one {# rule} other {# rules}}.
wireguard.agent.ingress.comfort.prune-hi: Hits only count NEW connections: long-lived sessions (LDAP, IMAP, iSCSI) look idle. Switched-off rules can be switched on again at any time.
wireguard.agent.ingress.confirm-open: Turn the ingress filter off? All traffic from the tunnel then reaches this network unfiltered — the rules only count hits. A separation between sites on the hub stays in place.
wireguard.agent.ingress.confirm-restrict: Turn the ingress filter on? All traffic forwarded from the tunnel into the LAN that does not match an active rule will be dropped — a missing rule cuts the site off for that traffic. Services on the gateway itself are not filtered.
wireguard.agent.ingress.danger.orphan: The WireGuard connection of this agent no longer exists – it can only be removed here.
wireguard.agent.ingress.danger.text: Revokes this site's agent: its token stops working at once and the gateway is no longer managed from here. Meant for sites that no longer exist.
wireguard.agent.ingress.danger.title: Remove agent
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.blocked.a: One of the agents no longer exists.
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.blocked.n: One side is set to "Freigaben only" and the partner masquerades into the direct tunnel: its traffic would come from the transfer net instead of the hub address and be dropped. Turn masquerading off on the partner.
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.blocked.s: both agents belong to the same site
One of the agents is not bound to a site link.
The sites are separated ("sites among each other") — the direct link stays down while the separation exists.
transfer net or endpoint overlaps a site or tunnel network – choose another /30 or endpoint
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.check.age: An agent does not report (A: {a}, B: {b}) – check the gateway and the agent service.
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.check.dns: {host} does not resolve – check the DynDNS entry.
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.check.ena: The link is off – port forward and path can only be checked once it is on.
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.check.end: The endpoint {endpoint} differs from the site's stored address ({stored}).
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.check.key: Keys are still missing – do both agents run version 1.6.0 or newer?
Both sides have exchanged their keys.
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.check.pat: Both sides use the direct path ({rtt} ms).
Both sides use the direct path.
Only one side uses the direct path, the other still the hub.
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.check.por: No handshake on the direct path – check the port forward UDP {port} to the gateway on side A's router (and that the line accepts incoming traffic, no CGNAT).
The direct tunnel is up (last handshake {age} s ago) – the port forward UDP {port} worked when it was built. Whether it survives a restart of the other side only shows on the next build.
Port forward cannot be checked while the link is off.
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.check.pub: The site comes from {seen}, but the endpoint points to {ips} – DynDNS stale or wrong address.
The site really comes from {seen} – matches the endpoint.
The site's public IP is unknown (the hub sees no endpoint).
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.delete-te: Both agents tear the tunnel down and forget their key. Traffic then goes through the hub again.
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.empty: No direct link yet. Without one, all traffic between sites goes through the hub.
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.form.agen: The site with a fixed public IP / port forward.
May have a changing IP, it connects to A.
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.form.enab: Turned on (only turn on after checking the configuration)
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.form.endp: IPv4 address or DNS name (a name is re-resolved for changing IPs).
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.form.name: Name
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.form.nat: {site} masquerades outgoing (as through the hub today)
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.form.nat-: Tick when the site masquerades into the hub tunnel today (e.g. a rule "-o wg0 -j MASQUERADE"). Firewalls, RADIUS and AD on the other side then see the same senders as before.
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.form.port: The router of {site} needs a port forward: UDP {port} → {ip}. You set it up there yourself; it is not part of FloppyGuard.
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.form.subn: A private /30 of its own that overlaps no site network and no tunnel network.
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.key-chang: A gateway reports a new key (re-install – or a stolen agent token). Until confirmed the old key stays valid, traffic goes through the hub.
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.lead: Two sites talk to each other directly instead of through the hub. If the direct link fails, traffic automatically goes through the hub again. Source addresses (NAT) stay as they are through the hub, and the Freigaben apply on both paths.
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.side.no-k: no key reported yet (agent 1.6.0 or newer needed)
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.sites.dyn: Does this line's IP change? Enter a DynDNS name, otherwise the link breaks on an IP change.
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.sites.lea: What the routers at the sites must be set up with. The public address (DynDNS name or fixed IP) is suggested as the endpoint of new direct links and checked here against the IP the site really comes from.
wireguard.agent.ingress.direct.title: Direct links
wireguard.agent.ingress.empty.text: A rule lets a source – the reverse proxy on the hub, another site or VPN clients – reach specific targets and ports in this network. While the filter is off, rules only count hits.
wireguard.agent.ingress.empty.text-restr: The filter is on – without a rule nothing gets through right now. Create the first rule.
wireguard.agent.ingress.empty.title: No rules yet
wireguard.agent.ingress.err.invalid-port: Invalid port entry: {value} (format tcp/443, udp/53 or tcp/8000:8010)
wireguard.agent.ingress.field.destinatio: IPv4 addresses or CIDRs in the site LAN — empty = all targets.
wireguard.agent.ingress.field.name: Name
wireguard.agent.ingress.field.name-auto-: Leave empty to name the rule after what it allows.
wireguard.agent.ingress.field.ports-hint: e.g. tcp/443, udp/53, tcp/8000:8010 — or tick “All ports”.
wireguard.agent.ingress.field.sources-hi: IPv4 addresses or CIDRs, comma or newline separated (at least one).
wireguard.agent.ingress.form.broad: This rule opens every port or the whole site — check that this is intended.
wireguard.agent.ingress.hit.stale: no new connection for more than 30 days — long-lived connections (e.g. LDAP, IMAP) are not counted, check before deleting
wireguard.agent.ingress.list.warnings: {count, plural, one {# proxy target is dropped} other {# proxy targets are dropped}}
wireguard.agent.ingress.open-hint: Before removing an external filter on the gateway (e.g. VPN_MGR): turn the ingress filter on and wait until the agent reports it as applied.
wireguard.agent.ingress.page.lead: Decide per site which traffic from the VPN tunnel may enter its local network.
wireguard.agent.ingress.page.title: Access rules
wireguard.agent.ingress.picker.no-option: Nothing found — type an IP or CIDR
wireguard.agent.ingress.result.reenabled: Rule “{name}” was switched off and is switched on again.
wireguard.agent.ingress.sentence.anythin: may access everything in the site – {ports}
wireguard.agent.ingress.sites.action.all: Click to allow the connection again
wireguard.agent.ingress.sites.adopt-text: The blocks between sites that were set by hand on the hub are saved as site separations in FloppyGuard. Traffic does not change. Afterwards the manual rules can be removed on the hub – only then can the separation be lifted here again.
wireguard.agent.ingress.sites.also-manua: also blocked by hand on the hub
wireguard.agent.ingress.sites.applied-er: Applying failed ({time}) – the hub keeps the previous rules.
wireguard.agent.ingress.sites.clients-un: Applies to site links only; VPN devices (clients) are not affected.
wireguard.agent.ingress.sites.confirm-al: {a} and {b} will be able to reach each other again – as far as the rules at each site allow.
Note: a rule set by hand on the hub also blocks this connection. It stays until it is removed there.
Allow the connection between {a} and {b} again?
wireguard.agent.ingress.sites.confirm-bl: {a} and {b} will no longer be able to reach each other – in both directions, immediately; open connections drop as well.
wireguard.agent.ingress.sites.dropped: {count, plural, one {{packets} packet dropped} other {{packets} packets dropped}}
wireguard.agent.ingress.sites.error.link: No stored separation matches an existing site link (WireGuard data empty or links re-created). So that nothing is opened by accident, the hub keeps the previous rules. Please set the separations again here.
wireguard.agent.ingress.sites.lead: The hub drops all traffic between separated sites – regardless of the ingress filter at the site. Applies to site links only; VPN devices (clients) are not affected.
wireguard.agent.ingress.sites.matrix-cap: Which sites are separated from each other (each pair once)
wireguard.agent.ingress.sites.summary: {blocked, plural, =0 {{total, plural, one {The site pair is not separated} other {None of the # site pairs separated}}} other {# of {total} site pairs separated}}
wireguard.agent.ingress.sites.switch-hin: Switch on = not separated (the site rules apply), off = separated on the hub.
wireguard.agent.ingress.sites.title: Separation between sites (on the hub)
wireguard.agent.ingress.sites.too-few: There are fewer than two site-to-site links – nothing to separate.
wireguard.agent.ingress.sites.warning.bo: After a hub restart the separation only takes effect again once FloppyGuard is running – the firewall's boot configuration does not load it yet.
wireguard.agent.ingress.sites.warning.li: A stored separation refers to a link that no longer exists – it is skipped and removed on the next save.
